headline: Core contracts verified on Etherscan with recognised-firm audit coverage through Feb 2025; some post-audit version drift unquantified
short_headline: Verified; multi-firm audits; minor drift risk

findings.text: StrategyManager proxy (0x858646372CC42E1A627fcE94aa7A7033e7CF075A) is a TransparentUpgradeableProxy verified on Etherscan (ABI source: etherscan). Its current implementation resolves to 0x88582996b70FDd7C4f16e3Fde7B53858FcE0d394, which is also independently verified on Etherscan (ABI source: etherscan), running version 1.12.0. DelegationManager proxy (0x39053D51B77DC0d36036Fc1fCc8Cb819df8Ef37A) is also verified on Etherscan as a TransparentUpgradeableProxy pointing to implementation 0xE7022a128Acd4C6cad7aFf6FA874D61f984BcE75 (version 1.9.0).

The public GitHub repository https://github.com/Layr-Labs/eigenlayer-contracts is referenced directly from the official EigenCloud website and EigenLayer documentation. The ABI structure (BUSL-1.1 license, contract naming, version strings) matches the known public repo structure. No commit SHA was pinned this run because GitHub direct fetches were blocked; recorded in unknowns.

The official audit page at docs.eigencloud.xyz/eigenlayer/security/audits references Certora and links to audit repositories on GitHub. Third-party data (CertiK Skynet) corroborates an extensive audit history: Sigma Prime (Jan 2025, Sep 2024, Aug 2024, May 2024, Feb 2024, May 2023 x2), Certora formal verification of EigenLayer Slashing (Jan 10 – Feb 11, 2025), ConsenSys Diligence (Apr 2023), Code4rena (Jul 2023). Most recent audits (Sigma Prime Jan 2025, Certora Feb 2025) cover the slashing/delegation architecture introduced in v1.x. Dedaub also audited the middleware in Feb 2024.

Auditing firms include Sigma Prime, Certora, ConsenSys Diligence, and Code4rena — all broadly recognised in the Solidity ecosystem. Sigma Prime is explicitly listed as having audited the core slashing and delegation logic.

StrategyManager is at version 1.12.0 and DelegationManager at 1.9.0 per live on-chain reads. The most recent audits completed in Jan–Feb 2025. Version bumps since then are noted but diff content was not sampled this run (GitHub blocked). Neither BurnOrRedistributableShares logic nor withdrawal delay contracts show any obvious new fund-flow functions relative to the audited slashing architecture visible in the ABI. Recorded in unknowns as an unquantified drift risk rather than a confirmed downgrade signal.

The StrategyManager proxy (0x858646372) points to implementation 0x88582996b70FDd7C4f16e3Fde7B53858FcE0d394, which is independently verified (ABI source: etherscan). The DelegationManager proxy points to implementation 0xE7022a128Acd4C6cad7aFf6FA874D61f984BcE75; this implementation address was surfaced on-chain but its Etherscan verification was not independently confirmed this run (recorded in unknowns). Etherscan's own record for the DelegationManager proxy shows 'ABI for the implementation contract at 0xe7022a128...', implying Etherscan auto-resolved and labelled the implementation as DelegationManager, which is consistent with it being verified.

steelman.red: If the DelegationManager implementation (0xE7022a128) is not independently verified on Etherscan, a core fund-custody contract would be effectively unverified, warranting red.
steelman.orange: StrategyManager is at v1.12.0 and DelegationManager at v1.9.0 while the most recent comprehensive audits ended Feb 2025; without a diff confirming no material fund-flow changes, the gap from the audited commit could justify orange.
steelman.green: Both sampled proxy+implementation pairs show Etherscan-sourced ABIs, indicating bytecode verification; multiple audits from top-tier firms (Sigma Prime, Certora) covered the slashing and delegation architecture as recently as Feb 2025, and the public Layr-Labs GitHub repo structurally matches the deployed source.

rationale.verdict: Choosing green because: (1) StrategyManager proxy and its implementation are both confirmed verified via defipunkd surfacer (ABI source: etherscan) in this run; (2) Etherscan's own proxy-resolution text for DelegationManager names its implementation as 'DelegationManager', consistent with verification; (3) multiple top-tier firms (Sigma Prime, Certora) audited the slashing/delegation architecture as recently as Jan–Feb 2025; (4) version drift cannot be confirmed as material without a diff that was inaccessible this run, so it is recorded in unknowns rather than used as a downgrade signal per V5 rules. The orange steelman is weaker because V5 requires naming a specific behavioral change, which was not observable this run.

protocol_metadata.about: EigenLayer (presented as EigenCloud's trust layer) is a restaking protocol on Ethereum where users stake Native ETH, Liquid Staking Tokens (LSTs), the EIGEN token, or other ERC-20s into smart contracts to extend Ethereum's cryptoeconomic security to Autonomous Verifiable Services (AVSs). Restakers deposit via the StrategyManager or EigenPodManager and delegate to Operators, who opt into AVSs and can be slashed for misbehavior through the AllocationManager. The protocol earns stakers rewards distributed by the RewardsCoordinator while enabling AVS developers to bootstrap security without building their own validator networks.
